title: Unit 5 – Trains
content:
A: Where did you go on your holiday?
B: I went to Bagan with my parents.
A: (1) How was it? Did you have a good time?
B: (2) It was wonderful. Bagan is a great city with many historical landmarks.
A: What places did you visit?
B: We visited many ancient pagodas, the museum and Tharabar Gate. (3) They are very interesting!
A: Really? Where did you stay there?
B: We stayed at the Florabreeze Hotel in Old Bagan.
A: (4) Was it expensive?
B: No, it was a budget hotel.
A: What about the food?
B: (5) The food was great! We had not only Myanmar traditional food but also European food, both of which were delicious.
A: Well. I may go to Bagan next holiday.

title: Unit 7 – Typical Myanmar Snacks
content:
A: My grandma hasn't been too well lately.
B: (1) What a pity! / Oh dear / That's too bad
A: She's 80. At her age, she should slow down a bit. But she said she would come along with us to Kyeik-htee-yo Pagoda.
B: (2) Did she? / Really? / That's amazing!
A: We told her to stay at home, but she won't listen to us. She said she wanted to enjoy her life to the full.
B: (3) That's great! / Fantastic!
A: Last week, she went to the supermarket and then cooked for the whole family.
B: (4) Really? / Did she? / That's amazing
A: We're going to give her a big party for her 81st birthday.
B: (5) Fantastic! / That's great / Lovely!
A: But she doesn't want us to spend much for her birthday. She prefers to make a donation to people who are in need.
B: That's very sweet of her.

title: Unit 9 – Climate Change
content:
A: Hey, did you hear that? A new parking site is going to be built in the park over there.
B: Really? But (1) In my opinion, that's crazy. What we need is more trees. (2) Personally, I think cars should disappear. They pollute the air and they make too much noise.
A: (3) The point is that we can't live without cars today. Without cars, how will you get to work?
B: I can take the bus.
A: Yes, (4) I know what you mean, but we use cars for so many purposes.
B: (5) That is very true, but we can always find other alternatives.
A: You have a point there, but if we didn't have cars, we would need better public transport.
B: Yes, (6) I agree.
A: But still, having a car is so convenient.
B: (7) Of course, I know. But we can't have everything, can we?
A: Exactly. (8) That's what I think too. We can't have everything. Still, so I prefer having a car.

title: Unit 10 – Food Safety
content:
A: (1) What fruits do you usually eat?
B: Oranges, bananas and apples.
A: Among them, which (2) do you like most and why?
B: Oranges most. I just love their taste.
A: (3) Do you think oranges are good for health?
B: Yes, I do as long as they contain no sweetener.
A: (4) How are oranges good for health?
B: They contain a lot of vitamins A and C, and they are good for the teeth.
A: (5) How often do you eat them?
B: Almost every day.
A: (6) Is there any kind of fruit you don't like?
B: Yes, dragon fruits. I don't find it tasty.

title: Unit 11 – THANAKA, Uniquely Myanmar
content:
Nu Nu: Hello, Thandar, where are you off to?
Thandar: The supermarket, to buy a few cosmetic items.
Nu Nu: Such as?
Thandar: Oh you know, lipstick, make-up, eye shadow, so on and so forth. (1) Would you care to come along?
Nu Nu: Yes, (2) I would, maybe just to keep you company and look around for a lipstick and eye shadow.
Thandar: (3) Why don't you buy creams or lotions to protect your skin from sun burn?
Nu Nu: (4) That sounds great, but I prefer our local product as it works fine for me.
Thandar: What do you mean by local product?
Nu Nu: Thanakha, of course. It beats all foreign products, and what's more, it is not expensive.
Thandar: Really?
Nu Nu: Of course. Have you ever seen my face turning oily? It's thanakha that keeps my complexion in good shape.
Thandar: Well, (5) that's a good idea, but I've never used it. I think I should try.
Nu Nu: You certainly should. And I guarantee that you'll come to prefer it to all those fancy foreign products!

title: Unit 12 – Urbanization
content:
Receptionist: Dr. Anderson's clinic. May I help you?
Patient: (1) I'd like to make an appointment with the doctor.
Receptionist: Certainly, could you tell me what your problem is?
Patient: (2) I'm not feeling very well.
Receptionist: OK, let me check. Yes, Dr. Anderson can see you tomorrow. Can you come in the morning?
Patient: (3) Certainly.
Receptionist: How about 10 o'clock?
Patient: (4) Yes, 10 o'clock is fine.
Receptionist: May I have your name?
Patient: (5) Nay Aung.
Receptionist: OK, 10 tomorrow morning.
Patient: (6) Thank you.
Receptionist: Goodbye.
